name: Sceptical extremes among the Sophists: Gorgias's nihilism
plain_explanation: One Sophist, Gorgias, pushed scepticism to an extreme: he argued nothing exists, that even if something did exist we could not know it, and that even if we could know it we could never explain it to anyone else.
precise_definition: Gorgias's three-part sceptical/nihilist thesis: (1) nothing exists; (2) if anything exists, it is unknowable; (3) even granting that one man could know it, he could never communicate it to others.
why_it_mattered: Illustrates, for Russell, the genuine intellectual rigor and willingness to follow argument to uncomfortable conclusions that he thinks characterized the best Sophists, in contrast to their popular reputation for mere cleverness or immorality.
competing_positions: Protagoras's more moderate relativism, which still preserves practical grounds for belief and action
